habitat: Evergreen forest and forested kloofs, foraging in the canopy and mid-stratum. SABAP1 describes the mid-stratum and canopy of mature evergreen temperate forest, including fairly small patches.
summary: A resident of evergreen forest, scarce in Kruger. Olive-green above, with a chestnut cap and eye-stripe, a yellow eyebrow and yellow breast, and a white belly. In southern birds the yellow extends onto the flanks and belly; in northern birds it is mainly on the throat. Sexes are alike. The immature has a greenish wash on the breast. The call is a plaintive tieuu, repeated for long periods, and the song is a high whistle, tirritee or sip sip sip pilly. Bill, eye, leg, wing and tail colours, and a flight pattern, were not described in the texts used here. No Kruger photograph was found. The population estimate was left unchanged.

similar.note: Willow Warbler has no chestnut cap or eye-stripe. It has a pale eyebrow and a notched tail, and it uses bush and woodland rather than evergreen forest.
Newman separates Yellow-throated Woodland Warbler from white-eyes by the chestnut cap and eye-stripe and by the forest habitat.
African Yellow Warbler is a bird of rank cover. Yellow-throated Woodland Warbler has a chestnut cap and eye-stripe and forages in evergreen forest.

underparts.pattern: Breast yellow and belly white. In southern birds the yellow extends onto the flanks and belly; in northern birds the yellow is confined mainly to the throat.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident of evergreen forest, and SABAP1 knows of no altitudinal migration in the eastern Transvaal, so status is resident. monthsPresent is unset. Avibase lists the Kruger occurrence as rare/accidental, and no month-by-month park list was published. The season table therefore follows the resident default, which is why this needs review. Sexes are alike. The immature is only the greenish wash on the breast. Bill, eye, legs, wings and tail were not given colours, and no flight pattern was described. No flight photograph and no Kruger photograph were found. The Garden Route pictures are the openly licensed South African frames that show the chestnut cap. Population figures were left unchanged.
